                            COMPREHENSIVE STIPULATION

       In accordance with 1.2.2.20(B) NMAC, Southwestern Public Service Company (“SPS”),

New Mexico Department of Justice (“NMDOJ”), New Mexico Large Customer Group

(“NMLCG”), Occidental Permian Ltd. (“OPL”), Louisiana Energy Services LLC (“LES”), Federal

Executive Agencies (“FEA”), Targa Resources Corp. (“Targa”), Walmart Inc. (“Walmart”),

Coalition for Clean Affordable Energy (“CCAE”), and Prosperity Works (collectively, the

“Signatories”) enter into this Comprehensive Stipulation (“Stipulation”). Commission Utility

Division Staff (“Staff”) does not oppose parts of the Stipulation, which it will articulate in its

Statement of Opposition. The New Mexico Energy, Minerals, and Natural Resources Department

(“EMNRD”) takes no position on the Stipulation. This Stipulation resolves all issues among the

Signatories concerning SPS’s Application for Revision of its Retail Rates under Advice Notice

341 and Other Associated Relief (“Application”), subject to the terms set forth below.




                                                1
                                           Background

       On November 20, 2025, SPS filed its Application in this proceeding. SPS requested

authorization to revise its New Mexico retail rates under Advice Notice 341 and requested other

associated relief. SPS’s Application sought a base rate revenue increase for the New Mexico retail

jurisdiction of $175,354,544, a 24.25% increase over current base rate revenue and 16.73%

increase in total revenues, based on a total New Mexico retail revenue requirement of

$892,652,373.

       SPS filed a Comprehensive List of Revisions on March 20, 2026, reflecting a net decrease

to SPS’s Future Test Year revenue deficiency of $3,054,395. On March 25, 2026, SPS submitted

notice of a correction to its Future Test Year depreciation expense, which reduced total company

depreciation expense by $11,833,081, reduced New Mexico retail depreciation expense by

$4,955,448, and reduced SPS’s New Mexico retail Future Test Year revenue requirement by

$4,748,791.

       The Signatories have engaged in settlement discussions and enter into this Stipulation to

resolve all issues concerning SPS’s Application. The Signatories agree that this Stipulation

represents a fair, just, and reasonable resolution of the issues addressed in this proceeding, is

consistent with the public interest, and should be approved by the Commission without

modification.

                                            Recitals

       The Signatories acknowledge and affirm the following matters:

       A.       SPS filed its Application using a Future Test Year running from December 1, 2026,

through November 30, 2027.




                                                2
        B.       Pursuant to 1.2.2.16 NMAC, the Signatories participated in extensive settlement

negotiations to resolve the issues raised in this proceeding. The Signatories who participated in

these settlement negotiations are knowledgeable and sophisticated parties and are well-informed

on the issues raised by SPS’s Application, supporting testimony, exhibits, discovery responses,

and the testimony filed by Staff and intervenors. The Signatories represent a diverse group of

stakeholders with a wide range of positions on the issues presented in this proceeding.

       C.       This Stipulation is the result of good-faith, arm’s-length negotiation, settlement,

and accommodation among the Signatories with respect to the issues presented in this case. The

Signatories agree that the stipulated resolution provides benefits to SPS, customers, and the public;

supports SPS’s continued provision of safe and reliable service; and reasonably resolves the issues

addressed by this Stipulation. The Signatories further agree that this Stipulation is fair, just,

reasonable, consistent with the public interest, and should be approved by the Commission without

modification.

                                           Agreements

       By this Stipulation, the Signatories agree to the following matters.

         I.     Stipulated Agreements Regarding SPS’s Application

                1.1    Base Rate Increase

       The Signatories agree that SPS should be authorized to implement an increase in New

Mexico retail base rate revenues of $90,000,000, effective December 1, 2026.

       The Signatories agree to the following New Mexico retail cost-of-service components

associated with the stipulated base rate increase:

       (a)      The stipulated return on equity (“ROE”) is 9.5%.




                                                 3
        (b)     The stipulated tax-unadjusted weighted average cost of capital (“WACC”) is

               7.59%.

       (c)     The stipulated capital structure consists of 54.7% common equity and 45.3% long-

               term debt.

       (d)     SPS’s cash working capital balance is $0, which is 0% of rate base.

       The base rate revenue increase by class and revenue proof is provided in Exhibit A to the

Stipulation (“Exhibit A”), and the rate tariffs and all other stipulated tariff changes are provided in

Exhibit B (“Exhibit B”). Depreciation rates are provided in Exhibit C to the Stipulation (“Exhibit

C”), and reconciliation statements are provided in Exhibit D (“Exhibit D”).

       Except as specifically noted above, the stipulated base rate revenue increase is not

associated with any specific calculation involving any of the stated cost of service components

herein, or approval or disapproval of any other issue raised in this case. The Signatories arrived at

the stipulated base rate revenue increase through a compromise of the various issues raised in this

case without specifically accepting or rejecting for purposes of this Stipulation any ratemaking

issue or principle other than those specified herein.

               1.2      Depreciation Rates and Service-Life Extensions

       The Signatories agree that SPS’s proposed depreciation rates should be adjusted to reflect

a net impact to the revenue deficiency of $0.

        The Signatories agree to the following service-life extensions:

        (a)    Extend the service life of Jones Unit 1 from 2031 to 2045;

        (b)    Extend the service life of Jones Unit 2 from 2034 to 2045;

        (c)    Extend the service life of Nichols Unit 1 from 2028 to 2035;

        (d)    Extend the service life of Nichols Unit 2 from 2027 to 2036;



                                                  4
            (e)   Extend the service life of Nichols Unit 3 from 2030 to 2042;

           (f)   Extend the service life of Maddox Unit 1 from 2028 to 2038;

           (g)   Extend the service life of Maddox Unit 2 from 2025 to 2043;

           (h)   Extend the service life of Plant X Unit 4 from 2027 to 2039; and

           (i)   Extend the service lives of Tolk Units 1 and 2 from December 2027 to March 2028.

SPS’s updated depreciation rates are included in Exhibit C.

                 1.3     Direct Assignment of Cunningham BESS

       The Signatories agree that SPS should be authorized to assign all costs and capacity

benefits of the Cunningham Battery Energy Storage System (“Cunningham BESS”) to SPS’s New

Mexico retail customers.

       SPS shall modify its jurisdictional allocator based on an agreed-upon valuation

methodology for the accredited capacity (“ACAP”) benefits of the Cunningham BESS. The

valuation methodology shall calculate the net ACAP benefit by adjusting the seasonal

Cunningham BESS ACAP for the applicable seasonal planning reserve margin (“PRM”), as

follows:

       (a)       Summer Period (May through October): The Cunningham BESS ACAP value

                 assigned to New Mexico shall equal the summer Cunningham BESS ACAP divided

                 by one plus the applicable summer PRM.

       (b)       Winter Period (November through April): The Cunningham BESS ACAP value

                 assigned to New Mexico shall equal the winter Cunningham BESS ACAP divided

                 by one plus the applicable winter PRM.

       This methodology is specific to this proceeding and is not precedential. SPS shall initiate

a stakeholder process to evaluate the treatment of directly assigned resources and the jurisdictional



                                                 5
 allocation of divergent state resource portfolios for future proceedings prior to filing its next base

rate case, and shall report on recommendations from this stakeholder evaluation in its next base

rate case.

               1.4     Interim Recovery of BESS Long-Term Purchased Power Agreement
                       Costs

        SPS withdraws, without prejudice, its request to temporarily recover through its Fuel and

Purchased Power Cost Adjustment Clause (“FPPCAC”) the capacity costs associated with the

BESS long-term purchased power agreements approved in Case No. 25-00085-UT. SPS has

removed the capacity costs associated with the BESS long-term purchased power agreements from

this settlement and may request recovery of those costs through the FPPCAC in a future

proceeding. The Signatories reserve the right to take any position in that future proceeding.

               1.5     SPS Short-Term Capacity Needs

        SPS withdraws, without prejudice, its request to recover Southwest Power Pool (“SPP”)

deficiency payments through the FPPCAC.

        SPS will use its best efforts to address short-term capacity needs, including, where prudent,

pursuing short-term capacity purchases in lieu of making SPP deficiency payments. Any such

capacity purchases or SPP deficiency payments incurred through the effective date of new rates

resulting from SPS’s next base rate case will be deferred and recorded as a regulatory asset.

        SPS may seek to recover the deferred costs in a future proceeding, subject to an annual cap

of $10 million for the New Mexico jurisdiction. The Signatories reserve the right to take any

position regarding the recovery or reasonableness of such deferrals in any future proceeding.

               1.6     Recovery Mechanisms for Variable Costs

        SPS withdraws its requests for a property tax tracker and an Excess Liability Insurance

expense tracker.


                                                  6
                 1.7       Recovery of Previously Approved Regulatory Assets and Deferrals

        The Signatories agree that SPS should be authorized to recover the following previously

approved regulatory assets and fixed deferrals:

        (a)     A three-year amortization of deferred Excess Liability Insurance (“ELI”) premiums

                approved in Case No. 25-00030-UT;

        (b)     A four-year amortization of the remaining investment in legacy meters approved in

                Case No. 22-00178-UT; and

        (c)     A four-year amortization of Community Solar Program costs, including regulatory

                and information technology expenses approved in Case No. 23-00071-UT.

        The Signatories agree that if new rates become effective in any subsequent rate case before

SPS has fully amortized any of the regulatory assets or fixed deferrals identified in this Section

1.7, SPS may include the then-unamortized balance in that rate case for continued recovery.

                1.8       Treatment of Federal Tax Credits

        The Signatories agree that SPS should be authorized to implement the following treatment

of federal tax credits.

                          A.    Production Tax Credits for SPS Solar Projects

        SPS may earn a return at the cost of long-term debt, through its FPPCAC, on its Deferred

Tax Asset (“DTA”) associated with production tax credits (“PTCs”) created by Plant X Solar,

Cunningham I Solar, and Cunningham II Solar (collectively, the “SPS Solar Projects”), to the

extent those PTCs are unused or not yet transferred.

        Should federal law allowing transferability materially change, SPS reserves the right to

seek different treatment of the PTCs for these facilities in a future proceeding. The PTC DTA

attributable to the SPS Solar Projects shall be excluded from rate base in future base rate

proceedings.

                                                  7
                        B.     Investment Tax Credits for Cunningham BESS and Plant X
                              BESS
       SPS is authorized to treat the investment tax credits (“ITCs”) for the Cunningham BESS

and Plant X BESS as follows:

       (a)    SPS shall amortize the value of the ITCs over five years to reduce SPS’s revenue

              requirement. The Cunningham BESS ITC amortization will begin in December

              2026 in alignment with new rates, and the Plant X BESS ITC amortization will

              begin upon the Plant X BESS commercial operation date.

       (b)    SPS shall amortize Cunningham BESS transfer costs, capped at 10% of the

              corresponding ITCs’ nominal value, over the same amortization period as the ITC

              value.

       (c)    SPS is authorized to accrue a regulatory asset associated with Plant X BESS transfer

              costs, capped at 10% of the corresponding ITCs’ nominal value, for future recovery.

       (d)    SPS may apply a return at the stipulated WACC to the unamortized balance of the

              ITC value and transfer costs.

                       C.      PTC Transfer Costs for Hale and Sagamore

       SPS is authorized to recover transfer costs, capped at 10% of nominal value, for PTCs from

the Hale and Sagamore Wind Projects through SPS’s FPPCAC.

              1.9      Off-System Sales Margins from Cunningham and Plant X Solar
                       Projects

       SPS will not retain off-system sales margins from the Cunningham and Plant X Solar

Projects after cost recovery commences for each project. SPS maintains authority to retain off-

system sales margins for the Cunningham and Plant X Solar projects as well as the Cunningham

1 BESS between Commercial Operation Date and the commencement of cost recovery, in

accordance with the provisions of the Final Order in Case No. 24-00270-UT.


                                               8
                1.10    Rate Case Expenses

        The stipulated base rate increase includes recovery of $4,342,331 in requested rate case

expenses and previous regulatory proceeding expenses, to be recovered over two years. The

Signatories agree that SPS may seek authority to continue recovering these rate case expenses in

a future proceeding if the two-year period has not been completed before the effective date of rates

in a subsequent rate case.

               1.11    Revenue Allocation and Rate Design

        The Signatories agree that SPS shall allocate among rate classes all costs of production and

transmission, including Hale and Sagamore wind generation, on an average-and-excess demand

four-coincident-peak (“AED 4-CP”) basis.

        PTCs will be allocated on an energy basis. The system load factor used in the AED 4-CP

method uses the system single peak demand for the year (1CP).

        SPS will study the jurisdictional and retail impact of adjusting AED 4-CP transmission

allocators to remove behind-the-meter generation load in the cost allocation workshops agreed

upon in Case No. 25-00085-UT, and will report on the results of the study in its next base rate

case. The study will include, to the extent available, sufficient data to identify all behind-the-meter

generation load for customers in each of SPS’s jurisdictions, inclusive of both wholesale and retail

load.

        For purposes of settlement, the Signatories agree on the stipulated base rate revenue

allocation shown in Exhibit A. Except as otherwise stated, the stipulated base rate revenue

allocation is not associated with any specific methodology, or approval or disapproval of any other

issue regarding class cost of service or revenue allocation raised in this case. The Signatories

reached the stipulated base rate revenue allocation through compromise of the issues raised in this



                                                  9
 case without specifically accepting or rejecting, for purposes of this Stipulation, any ratemaking

issue or principle.

               1.12   Electric Affordability Program

       The Signatories agree that SPS’s proposed Electric Affordability Program (“EAP”) should

be approved subject to the following terms:

       (a)     SPS shall update its affordability and budget analysis and evaluate whether the

               $750,000 annual budget is sufficient under current proposed rates. SPS shall

               provide the analysis in its next base rate case.

       (b)     SPS shall make a one-time shareholder contribution of $750,000 to improve

               program reach, supplement benefits, or support outreach and administration.

       (c)     SPS shall convene an EAP collaborative working group within 60 days after

               approval of this Stipulation to evaluate implementation, data, reporting, eligibility,

               budget sufficiency, cost recovery, and future modifications. Recommendations

               from the working group will be included in SPS’s next base rate case.

       (d)     SPS shall coordinate EAP implementation with other low-income programs,

               including energy efficiency, weatherization, LIHEAP, and customer outreach

               resources.

               1.13   Rate Design and Tariff Issues

       SPS will modify the current Large General Service Transmission (“LGS-T”) 60% ratchet

demand to a 70% ratchet demand.

       SPS will continue to provide its power factor credit for the LGS-T class.

       All other rate design aspects of SPS’s proposed tariffs are approved, except as stated in

Section 1.16 regarding Standby Rate 85. Except as otherwise stated, the stipulated rate design is

not associated with any specific methodology, or approval or disapproval of any other issue

                                                 10
 regarding class cost of service or rate design raised in this case. The Signatories reached the

stipulated rate design through compromise of the issues raised in this case without specifically

accepting or rejecting, for purposes of this Stipulation, any ratemaking issue or principle.

       The rate tariffs and all other stipulated tariff changes are provided in Exhibit B.

               1.14    Renewable*Connect Tariff

       SPS will exclude costs recovered in base rates from any Renewable*Connect

administrative charges.

       The Renewable*Connect Unbundled Production Credit will be equivalent to the demand

charge less the Unbundled Transmission Demand Charges. SPS will subtract the Unbundled

Transmission Demand Charge, which is calculated as part of the Standby service rates, from the

standard LGS-T 115 kV winter and summer demand charges.

               1.15    Time-of-Use Fuel Pilot

       The Signatories agree that SPS’s proposed time-of-use (“TOU”) fuel pilot is reasonable

and should be approved.

               1.16    Standby Rate 85

       The standby generation demand charge will continue to be designed equal to 10% of the

applicable LGS-T generation demand rate.

       SPS will correct the proposed Rate 85 rate design to maintain consistency with the existing

Option 1 rate structure, under which total revenues from standby demand and backup energy

charges would be the same for a customer with no onsite solar production as they would be under

Rate 34.

               1.17    Jurisdictional Allocation

       SPS will adjust the 12-coincident-peak (“12-CP”) production jurisdictional system

allocator to remove the New Mexico load served by the accredited capacity of the Cunningham

                                                 11
 BESS from the shared system capacity pool used to allocate shared system production resources.

This adjustment will reflect the direct assignment of the Cunningham BESS to New Mexico and

the agreed valuation of the Cunningham BESS capacity benefit assigned to New Mexico as

described in Section 1.3.

               1.18    WAPA Credits

       The credits included in the SLCA Rider No. 27 shall be set equal to the production capacity

costs included in the LGS-T 115 kV demand and energy charges.

               1.19    Public Electric Vehicle Direct Current Fast Charging Rate

       SPS agrees to collaborate with Walmart and other interested stakeholders regarding the

development of a new electric vehicle rate specifically designed for public-facing direct current

fast charging (“DCFC”) facilities.

       SPS shall initiate a stakeholder process within 60 days following the Commission’s final

order in this proceeding and report on that process in its next Transportation Electrification Plan

filing. Based on those workshops, SPS shall file a proposed DCFC-specific rate, tariff, or rate

design with the Commission.

               1.20    Data Centers and Large Load Tariffs

       SPS shall develop and file for Commission approval a new Large Load customer class and

tariff within six months following the Commission’s final order in this proceeding and include the

Large Load customer class in its cost-of-service study in its next base rate case, to the extent that

such a tariff is approved by the Commission prior to the filing of that next base rate case.

       The proposed class and tariff shall be designed to ensure that all costs attributable to serving

Large Load customers are assigned to that class and do not shift costs or risks to any other customer

class. SPS will gather intervenor input on the Large Load tariff before filing it.



                                                 12
          II.    Stipulated Agreements Regarding Miscellaneous Matters

                2.1    Obligation to Actively Support Stipulation

        The Signatories agree that they will affirmatively support this Stipulation and undertake

reasonable and good-faith efforts before the Commission to obtain approval of this Stipulation.

                2.2    Granting Waivers, Variances, and Other Approvals

        To the extent additional waivers, variances, or approvals are required to implement this

Stipulation as approved by the Commission, the Signatories support the Commission granting

those waivers, variances, and approvals.

                2.3    Reconciliation Statement and Supporting Attachments

        This Stipulation is accompanied by a reconciliation statement showing the dollar impact of

the settlement and the resulting rates, as required by 1.2.2.20 NMAC. The reconciliation statement

contains or attaches the information required by 1.2.2.36(F) NMAC and is included as Exhibit D

to this Stipulation.

        The Signatories support approval of the rates, tariff sheets, depreciation rates, and other

materials necessary to implement this Stipulation, as reflected in Exhibits A through D.

                2.4    Admission of Pre-Filed Testimony and Other Filings into Record

        The Signatories support the admission into the record of all pre-filed direct testimony and

attachments.

                2.5    Position of CCAE and Prosperity Works

        CCAE and Prosperity Works do not stipulate to the terms in Section 1.1 (Base Rate

Increase) or Section 1.11 (Revenue Allocation and Rate Design) but do not contest those terms or

seek modification of those terms in this proceeding. Nothing in this Section 2.5 limits CCAE’s or

Prosperity Works’ support for the remaining terms of this Stipulation or their agreement that the

Stipulation should be approved without modification.

                                                13
                2.6     Position of Staff

       Staff is not a Signatory to the Stipulation. Staff does not oppose parts of the Stipulation,

which it will articulate in its Statement of Opposition.

               2.7     Effect and Limitation of Stipulation

       (a)     This Stipulation results from negotiation, compromise, and settlement among the

               Signatories. It resolves the issues concerning SPS’s Application in this proceeding

               as among the Signatories. The Signatories agree that this Stipulation is the product

               of serious bargaining among capable, knowledgeable parties; benefits customers

               and the public interest; does not violate any important regulatory principle or

               practice; represents a fair, just, and reasonable resolution of the issues addressed by

               this Stipulation; and should be approved by the Commission without modification.

               This Stipulation does not bind Staff or any other non-signatory.

       (b)     The provisions of this Stipulation are interdependent and not severable. None of the

               provisions becomes operative unless the Commission approves the Stipulation in

               its entirety. If the Commission issues an order inconsistent with this Stipulation,

               any Signatory may withdraw from the Stipulation and advocate any position it

               considers appropriate on the issues addressed in this Stipulation.

       (c)     This Stipulation binds the Signatories only for purposes of resolving the issues in

               this proceeding. Except as expressly provided here, the Stipulation is not binding

               or precedential in any other proceeding. A Signatory’s support of the Stipulation

               may differ from positions it has taken or may take in other cases before the

               Commission. Nothing in this Stipulation waives any claim or position a Signatory

               may assert in another proceeding.

       (d)     This Stipulation binds and benefits the Signatories and their successors and assigns.

                                                 14
                 2.8     Multiple Counterparts

        This Stipulation may be executed in any number of counterparts, including by electronic

means or PDF signature. Each counterpart will be deemed an original, and all counterparts together

constitute one and the same agreement.

        The Signatories agree that if, for any reason, the Hearing Examiners or Commission

determine that this Stipulation does not satisfy the Commission’s requirements for consideration

or approval of a stipulation, the Signatories will endeavor in good faith to remedy any deficiencies

and satisfy those requirements.

        If the Commission issues an order rejecting this Stipulation or modifying one or more terms

of this Stipulation in a way that is unacceptable to one or more Signatories, each Signatory shall

have the right to withdraw from this Stipulation and advocate any position it considers appropriate

to resolve this case.

        If this Stipulation is rejected and this matter must be resolved through litigation, the

Signatories agree to make good-faith efforts to complete the hearing process as expeditiously as

possible.

        The following fully and duly authorized representatives of the Signatories have signed this

Stipulation as of June 22, 2026.
